item.title: LeBron James heading to Philly in deal with 76ers
item.description: The Sixers' wild offseason continued Friday when they added four-time NBA champion LeBron James.

item.title: Upper West Side double stabbing suspect facing hate crime charges
item.description: The suspect in Thursday's double stabbing​ on New York City's Upper West Side has been charged with attempted murder as a hate crime, among other things.

item.title: Trump speaks at White House Correspondents' Dinner, in redo after April attack
item.description: President Trump is attending the redo of the White House Correspondents' Dinner on Friday night, after an armed assailant upended April's dinner.

item.title: Trump speaks at the rescheduled White House Correspondents' dinner
item.description: President Trump attended and spoke at the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner on Friday night at the Waldorf Astoria in Washington, D.C. The April correspondents' dinner was disrupted by an active shooter.

item.title: SpaceX's Super Heavy-Starship blasts off on 13th test flight
item.description: An upgraded version of the world's most powerful rocket is key to landing NASA astronauts on the moon in the agency's Artemis program.

item.title: 1.6 million cartons of eggs are recalled over potential salmonella contamination
item.description: The recall affects white-shell and cage-free eggs sold under multiple grocery brands in six states. No illnesses have been reported.

item.title: How a man's daily routine of ordering gumbo wound up saving his life
item.description: At the Shrimp Basket restaurant in Pensacola, Florida, a customer consistently ordered a cup of gumbo for lunch and for dinner for 10 years. When he didn't show up one week, the chef went to his house to check on him. Steve Hartman goes "On the Road" with the story, months later.

item.title: SpaceX launches 13th flight test of Starship rocket
item.description: SpaceX on Friday launched the 13th flight test of its Starship V3 rocket. CBS News space consultant Bill Harwood has the latest.

item.title: White House Correspondents' Association scholarship recipients relive terrifying dinner
item.description: Kaitlin Bender-Thomas and Madison Maynard, two White House Correspondents' Association scholarship recipients, join "The Daily Report" to reflect on April's terrifying shooting ahead of the rescheduled dinner.

item.title: Iran keeps targeting American bases as U.S. interceptor stockpiles dwindle
item.description: Explosions were heard near a U.S. base in Iraq, and Iran said it targeted Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait as the 21-week war intensifies.

item.title: How Jordan became a target for Iran in war with U.S.
item.description: Since the Iran war began in February, Jordan has largely avoided the kind of onslaught Tehran has aimed at places like Kuwait, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates. With recent attacks, and one that killed three U.S. soldiers, that's changed. CBS News senior national security correspondent Charlie D'Agata examines why.

item.title: Substance in work van of man killed by ICE tested negative for drugs, prosecutor says
item.description: A substance found in the work van of a Mexican immigrant killed by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent has tested negative for illicit drugs, the top prosecutor in Houston said Friday.

item.title: WHCA President Weijia Jiang speaks at rescheduled dinner 3 months after shooting
item.description: Outgoing president of the White House Correspondents' Association, Weijia Jiang, spoke at the dinner attended by journalists, politicians, and President Trump on Friday night. The event was rescheduled after a shooting attack disrupted the original dinner in April.

item.title: Trump flew from Turkey on older plane after credible threat from Iran and proxies
item.description: President Trump departed the NATO summit in Turkey on an old Air Force One jet following a credible threat from Iran and allied proxy groups, U.S. officials told CBS News.

item.title: Thousands expected to attend Comic-Con in San Diego as Johnny Depp crashes party
item.description: Comic-Con spokesperson David Glanzer joins "The Daily Report" to share more about the popular event happening now in San Diego as Johnny Depp crashes the convention to promote his upcoming film "Ebenezer."

item.title: Iran hits U.S. facilities in the Middle East as Trump is pressed on exit strategy
item.description: Iran fired at U.S. military facilities in the Middle East on Friday as President Trump launched a 13th consecutive night of strikes against the country on Thursday. Samantha Vinograd has more.

item.title: Trump orders signs placed outside Smithsonian warning of "inaccurate" information
item.description: President Trump ordered federal officials to install signs outside the National Museum of American History that correct what he says is "inaccurate" information presented by the institution about American history.

item.title: LeBron James to play for Philadelphia 76ers, calling it his "last decision"
item.description: LeBron James, one of the greatest players in NBA history, announced he is leaving the Los Angeles Lakers for the Philadelphia 76ers, a team that hasn't won a championship since 1983. Mark Strassmann reports.

item.title: Why are Americans so united against data centers?
item.description: During a time when Americans are mostly divided on the issues this election year, many are united around opposition to new data centers. Tony Dokoupil has "The Big Question."

item.title: Pentagon under fire for dropping tally of troops killed in Iran from 18 to 14
item.description: The Pentagon came under fire this week after its tally of the number of troops killed in the Iran war suddenly dropped from 18 to 14. Charlie D'Agata has more details on the discrepancy.

item.title: Apalachee High School shooting suspect pleads guilty to all charges
item.description: Colt Gray was charged with 55 counts, including malice murder, and faces life in prison without parole for the deadly mass shooting at Apalachee High School.

item.title: 7/24: CBS Evening News
item.description: A plane makes a crash landing off the Washington state coast; the Apalachee High School shooting suspect pleads guilty in a Georgia courtroom.

item.title: What Trump's new "forced labor" tariffs on 60 economies will mean for U.S. consumers
item.description: President Trump announced a new set of tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% on 60 trade partners over "forced labor" concerns on Thursday, just as Mr. Trump's temporary 10% levy was due to expire. Olivia Rinaldi explains what this means for consumers.

item.title: Ontario Premier Doug Ford on Trump's new tariff threat: "It's unfortunate he took this avenue"
item.description: The U.S. on Friday imposed a new 10% tariff on Canada, with 50% duties set to take effect later in August, significantly escalating trade tensions between the two countries. Ontario Premier Doug Ford joins "The Takeout" with his reaction.

item.title: Paramount to delay Warner Bros. merger until as late as June 2027
item.description: Paramount Skydance on Friday said it would delay the deal until as late as June 2027.

item.title: 7/24: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Tight security in place for White House Correspondents' Dinner as Trump set to attend; new tariff threat strains relationship between U.S. and Canada.

item.title: "The child is terrified": Doctors on front lines of measles comeback speak out
item.description: Confirmed measles cases in the U.S. just hit a 35-year high, and it's only July.

item.title: Pentagon website "anomalies" that removed names of 4 killed in Iran war remain
item.description: The Pentagon website, which was last updated on July 22, still showed only 14 killed in the conflict as of Friday.

item.title: Ford recalls more than half a million Bronco vehicles over engine fire risk
item.description: A short circuit in the engine compartment can potentially cause a fire. Here's the fix.

item.title: Cyclosporiasis outbreak traced to lettuce from Mexico used by Taco Bell
item.description: A lettuce supplier to fast-food giant Taco Bell has been linked to a nationwide cyclosporiasis outbreak that has sickened thousands of people, the CDC said.
